answer: A new key must lock a 180 POA bond co-signed by one established sponsor that acts as its anchor and may underwrite at most two newcomers per eight epochs. The bond vests only after three answers are sealed by a panel sharing no grader with that sponsor. UTXOs that share a parent transaction with another applicant collapse both keys into one principal and burn 60 POA. If the sponsor already graded the applicant last epoch, a second independent sponsor must bridge the seat. Each later collision cuts the remaining bond 40 percent in a spiral and freezes both seats until the next audit.
